original_test_intent: Verify that a defined PSU over-temperature condition is saved in the CRPS blackbox with the expected sensor/status identity, protection behavior and timeline.
original_method: A qualified operator uses a vendor-approved chamber/heating or safe simulation method on the identified thermal region while independent sensors and a hard cooling/cutoff path constrain the profile. The raw blackbox record is extracted and correlated with the measured temperatures and recovery.
manual_activity: A qualified engineer must identify the thermal target, establish the chamber/fixture and supervise heating/cooling. Agent automation may monitor and correlate evidence only after the approved profile exists.
required_inputs: PSU/DUT identity and exact internal sensor/region represented by the fault
Vendor threshold, ramp, dwell, tolerance, load condition and expected protection response
Approved chamber/thermal fixture or documented simulation, independent sensors and emergency cooling/cutoff
Blackbox extraction tool/schema and expected over-temperature fields
Operator, inspection/recovery plan and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not heat the PSU, obstruct cooling, manipulate fan control or write thresholds through an undocumented method.
Validate sensor placement, chamber/fixture limits, ramp/dwell and immediate cooling/cutoff before stimulus.
Preserve baseline logs and protect nearby hardware/load.
Stop for envelope exceedance, smoke, odor, damage, protection failure, unexpected shutdown or management loss.
No automatic repeat, alternate sensor/profile, reset or power cycle.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the approved thermal/evidence plan and collect baseline telemetry.
After operator-controlled stimulus, retain independent and PSU temperatures, load/protection timeline and raw blackbox export.
Correlate sensor threshold, event fields and cooling recovery.
Do not control unapproved heating or issue the verdict.
engineer_actions: Define/approve and supervise the thermal target/profile and fixture.
Operate emergency cooling/cutoff and inspect/recover hardware.
Provide inaccessible blackbox data and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It safely refuses direct execution but is not a method; its generic physical/AC language cannot define an over-temperature stimulus and its blackbox-access claim is unsupported.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the approved chamber/thermal-fixture SOP or documented vendor simulation plus the vendor blackbox extractor after profile and sensor semantics are fixed.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 5 and Machine Time 5 remain source facts; they do not define a ramp or dwell.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Select one documented thermal sensor/region, define ramp/dwell/abort limits, synchronize independent measurements, execute once under operator control, restore cooling and correlate the blackbox record.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the named PSU, sensor region, load and validated thermal fixture.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record PSU/BMC firmware, fixture controller, sensor calibration and blackbox schema/tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor OTP and blackbox documentation must be supplied; no threshold/profile is invented.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the over-temperature condition measurable and recoverable while preserving blackbox validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One sensor/profile does not cover other hotspots, ambient over-temperature or fan-fault paths.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Sensor, threshold/profile, load, fixture, monitoring/cooling, expected record and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Internal hotspots can rise faster than visible BMC sensors; external temperature alone may not prove the intended condition.

project_override_considerations: A project may select a chamber, local heater or vendor simulation only with documented equivalence to the intended blackbox sensor. Report sensor/profile coverage; do not substitute fan failure or generic stress.
expected_evidence: Approved sensor/profile/load, fixture and sensor calibration, safety checklist
Operator record and synchronized independent/PSU temperature, fan/load, protection and cooling timeline
Raw blackbox export with schema/tool version and expected OTP fields
Preserved platform logs plus inspection and thermal recovery evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and procedure consistently target blackbox capture of over-temperature. Missing sensor/profile and record fields are underspecification, not conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Sensor choice, thermal profile and safe stimulus define the operation and coverage. Guessing them can damage the PSU, so the case is genuinely BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree the agent must not improvise heating; reject its generic alternatives and unsupported blackbox limitation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with BLOCKED and the sensor/profile/monitoring/cooling/record/recovery gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates sensor-specific OTP evidence from fan fault or ambient heat and identifies automatable monitoring after setup.

review_improvement: This review defines the missing sensor and thermal envelope, preserves raw correlation and blocks unsafe inference of heating or threshold manipulation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Over-temperature has no executable meaning until the sensor/region, threshold, profile and safe method are known. These choices alter both hazard and blackbox signature; therefore their absence is a real BLOCKED condition, not a routine missing parameter.
